_removed.note: Nine rows present in USDA Foundation Foods were left out on purpose. Recorded here rather than deleted silently, so a later reader can see the decision instead of wondering about the gap.
_removed.watermelon_rind: Watermelon, seedless, rind only -- the white shell, not the flesh. No flesh row exists in Foundation Foods to sit beside it, so anybody searching 'watermelon' would have found the rind and logged 19 kcal for something they never ate.
_removed.egg_dried_and_frozen: Six rows. Dried egg white measures 376 kcal and 80 g protein per 100 g because it is powder; somebody picking it instead of the fresh row logs seven times what they ate. The three fresh rows remain.
_removed.kiwi_peeled: Kiwifruit, peeled -- 58.5 kcal against 58.0 for the unpeeled row. The same fruit twice; the unpeeled name is the one a person types.

_conventions.brackets: An Arabic name carries a second name in brackets only where a speaker somewhere would search by the other word and find nothing -- regional splits (شمندر/بنجر) and transliterations with a real Arabic alternative. Not spelling variants, not glosses, not explanations. About one name in eight.
_conventions.state_words: دry/canned/cooked appear in the name because the difference is threefold: chickpeas are 372 kcal dry and 133 canned.
_conventions.local_names: Where a language has its own name rather than a transliteration, that name is used: bartlett pear is Williams in French and German, Chilean sea bass is Légine australe, sweet and sour pork is 咕噜肉 in Chinese.
